title: Health Economic Analysis of Treatment Costs in Patients with Giant Cell Arteritis: Prednisolone Monotherapy versus Tocilizumab–Prednisolone Combination Therapy, with an Exploratory Evaluation of Upadacitinib
summary:
Background

Giant cell arteritis is an inflammatory disease of the blood vessels that mainly affects older adults. Treatment frequently involves prednisolone, a corticosteroid. However, prolonged use can cause substantial adverse effects. Additional medications, such as tocilizumab or upadacitinib, may help control the disease and reduce prednisolone requirements. Although these medications have higher acquisition costs, they may reduce costs associated with disease relapses and treatment-related complications. Their overall impact on treatment costs in the German healthcare setting remains insufficiently studied.

Research question

This study investigates differences in estimated treatment costs between tocilizumab plus prednisolone and prednisolone monotherapy. Disease control, relapses, prednisolone requirements and documented adverse effects will also be compared. Upadacitinib plus prednisolone will be assessed in an additional exploratory analysis.

Methods

This retrospective observational study will analyse existing medical records of approximately 300–400 adult patients with giant cell arteritis treated at University Hospital Bonn. Data from 2013 through 2026 will be included. Information collected will include medications and doses, treatment duration, disease course, examination findings, adverse effects and hospitalisations.

Treatment costs will be estimated from documented therapies and events using standardised treatment scenarios and German price lists and reimbursement schedules, and compared per patient-year. Individual billing data will not be analysed. Differences between treatment groups will be accounted for in the statistical analysis where the available data permit.

All treatment decisions were made independently of the study as part of routine clinical care. No additional examinations or treatment changes will take place. Data will initially be processed in pseudonymised form; only a dataset assessed as sufficiently anonymised will be provided for statistical analysis. The findings are intended to support the clinical and economic assessment of these treatment strategies.
